html:
The Mnicoujou, or Miniconjou, are one of the seven divisions of the Lakota, part of the Očhéthi Šakówiŋ or Sioux. Their name means planters by the water. In the 1800s they lived in western South Dakota, from the Black Hills to the Platte River.

Like other Lakota they lived as mounted bison hunters on the plains, moving camp with the herds. Their warriors fought with Crazy Horse in the wars of the 1860s and 1870s.

In December 1890, Spotted Elk, also called Big Foot, led a Miniconjou band toward Pine Ridge. The army stopped them at Wounded Knee Creek, and in the Wounded Knee Massacre soldiers killed about 250 to 300 men, women and children. Most Miniconjou today live on the Cheyenne River reservation, with the Itazipco and other Lakota.
